item.title: El alcahuete es peor que el autor.
🧩 The structural refusal of a shared timeline
item.description:
The collapse of the shared timeline

You try to pin down a date or an intent, and the talk does not resolve. It spins into chaos, while the fight you meant to finish sits under a stack of old complaints and stories that keep changing shape.

What you are watching is less a normal disagreement than two ways of seeing the same scene. One side thinks facts clear things up; the other treats that kind of clarity as something to dodge.

item.title: ℹ️ Why is sociopathy still a taboo?
item.description:
We treat sociopathy as a movie villain rather than a biological reality. We binge fiction about serial killers and crack jokes about “psychos” because it is easier than admitting some people never grow a “good” switch to flip.

Silence leaves families and kids without clear guidance. Parents often rely on abstract moralizing instead of practical rules. Adults who recognize their own lack of internal regulation often hide it.

When the guilt loop never wires in, internal pressure builds without a release mechanism. This often leads to externalized harm. The taboo prevents the practical solutions needed to manage this behavior.

item.title: 🔮 The prediction business sells obedience as foresight
item.description:
Surveillance got cheaper than East Germany

East Germany’s Stasi was expensive and human-heavy: it could only watch roughly a third of the population. Today’s stack is different. Phones, browsers, and platforms collect thousands of signals per person, cheaply, across whole populations.

“Nothing to hide” protects you from power, not guilt

Véliz flips the comfortable line (if you did nothing wrong, you have nothing to hide). Privacy limits what powerful actors can infer and do to you and to people connected to you.
